description: NL->SQL questions over the `cities` dataset (public/data/datasets.json): cities(name, country_code, feature_code, population BIGINT, elevation INTEGER in m (-9999 = unknown in 58 rows), timezone, lat, lon), 34,159 places with >= 15,000 inhabitants, and countries(code, name, continent, capital, area_km2, population, currency), 252 rows. No time column at all; many questions need the country join. Same scoring rules as evals/sql-corpus.json.

cases.question: 10 largest cities by population
reference: SELECT name, population FROM cities ORDER BY population DESC LIMIT 10
SELECT name, country_code, population FROM cities ORDER BY population DESC LIMIT 10

cases.question: which 10 countries have the most cities
reference: SELECT country_code, count(*) AS cities FROM cities GROUP BY country_code ORDER BY cities DESC LIMIT 10
SELECT k.name, count(*) AS cities FROM cities c JOIN countries k ON c.country_code = k.code GROUP BY k.name ORDER BY cities DESC LIMIT 10

cases.question: total city population per continent
cases.reference: SELECT k.continent, sum(c.population) AS population FROM cities c JOIN countries k ON c.country_code = k.code GROUP BY k.continent ORDER BY k.continent

cases.question: average city elevation per continent
reference: SELECT k.continent, avg(c.elevation) AS elevation FROM cities c JOIN countries k ON c.country_code = k.code GROUP BY k.continent ORDER BY k.continent
SELECT k.continent, avg(c.elevation) AS elevation FROM cities c JOIN countries k ON c.country_code = k.code WHERE c.elevation <> -9999 GROUP BY k.continent ORDER BY k.continent
SELECT k.continent, avg(c.elevation) AS elevation FROM cities c JOIN countries k ON c.country_code = k.code WHERE c.elevation > -9999 GROUP BY k.continent ORDER BY k.continent
cases.note: elevation -9999 marks an unknown value in GeoNames; filtering it is better, the naive average is accepted.

cases.question: Urban primacy: population of the largest city divided by the second largest, top 20 countries
reference: WITH r AS (SELECT country_code, population, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code ORDER BY population DESC) AS rn FROM cities), p AS (SELECT country_code, max(population) FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) / max(population) FILTER (WHERE rn = 2) AS primacy FROM r WHERE rn <= 2 GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) = 2) SELECT k.name AS country, primacy FROM p JOIN countries k ON p.country_code = k.code ORDER BY primacy DESC LIMIT 20

WITH r AS (SELECT country_code, population, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code ORDER BY population DESC) AS rn FROM cities), p AS (SELECT country_code, max(population) FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) / max(population) FILTER (WHERE rn = 2) AS primacy FROM r WHERE rn <= 2 GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) = 2) SELECT p.country_code AS country, primacy FROM p ORDER BY primacy DESC LIMIT 20

WITH r AS (SELECT country_code, population, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code ORDER BY population DESC) AS rn FROM cities), p AS (SELECT country_code, max(population) FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) / max(population) FILTER (WHERE rn = 2) AS primacy FROM r WHERE rn <= 2 GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) = 2 AND max(population) FILTER (WHERE rn = 2) > 0) SELECT k.name AS country, primacy FROM p JOIN countries k ON p.country_code = k.code ORDER BY primacy DESC LIMIT 20

WITH r AS (SELECT country_code, population, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code ORDER BY population DESC) AS rn FROM cities), p AS (SELECT country_code, max(population) FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) / max(population) FILTER (WHERE rn = 2) AS primacy FROM r WHERE rn <= 2 GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) = 2 AND max(population) FILTER (WHERE rn = 2) > 0) SELECT p.country_code AS country, primacy FROM p ORDER BY primacy DESC LIMIT 20
cases.note: Country by name or code. Ratio of rank 1 to rank 2 by population; a second city with population 0 (dirty data) gives infinity unless excluded.

cases.question: for each continent, the average share of a country's city population that lives in its largest city
reference: WITH c AS (SELECT country_code, max(population) / sum(population) AS share FROM cities GROUP BY 1) SELECT k.continent, avg(c.share) AS share FROM c JOIN countries k ON c.country_code = k.code GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH c AS (SELECT country_code, max(population) / sum(population) AS share FROM cities GROUP BY 1) SELECT k.continent, 100 * avg(c.share) AS share FROM c JOIN countries k ON c.country_code = k.code GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.note: Aggregate per country first, then average per continent; fraction or percent.

SELECT k.name AS country, c.name AS city FROM (SELECT name, country_code, population, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code ORDER BY population DESC) AS rn FROM cities) c JOIN countries k ON c.country_code = k.code WHERE k.continent = 'Europe' AND c.rn = 3 ORDER BY 1
